A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FakeShield framework and MMTD-Set. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures, prompts, and examples, support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original detection, localization, explanation, robustness, and ablation results in Tables 1–6 and accompanying figures and appendix examples.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds DeepFake comparisons, localization results, and appendix ablation and generalization experiments in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: FakeShield retains the same domain-tag generator, decoupled detection and localization modules, TCM/SAM pipeline, LoRA adaptation, and loss components. Appendix A.3 tests correction and input variants as ablations; it does not replace the proposed method. The Figure 3 input correction agrees with the tokenized input already specified in v3's Equation 3.

E1.justification: v4 adds Seq-DeepFake evaluation and tests images produced by previously unseen ControlNet and SDXL inpainting generators (Table 2 and Appendix A.4). It also adds DeepFake localization evaluation. These materially broaden the tested manipulation sources and generalization scenarios. DFFD is the existing FaceApp/FFHQ coverage under a clearer label, not another newly added dataset.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds Exposing and RECCE alongside CADDM and HiFi-DeepFake, including comparisons on the retained DFFD data. The general detection, localization, and explanation comparator sets remain unchanged. The new generator experiments reuse MVSS-Net, CAT-Net, and HiFi-Net rather than introducing further comparison methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include correction-supervised and alternative-input controls in Appendix A.3, plus testing on 2,000 newly constructed tampered images from unseen generators in A.4. Section 4.2 specifies retraining Exposing and RECCE. Existing metrics, thresholds, learning rates, and training epoch counts remain unchanged; omitted batch sizes do not establish an actual training-setting change.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3 adds controlled studies asking whether explicit correction of detector descriptions improves localization and which instruction, image, domain-tag, and description inputs are effective. Appendix A.4 adds unseen-generator generalization tests, and Table 6 extends the domain-tag ablation to IMD2020. These substantially expand the evidence probing the architecture and generalization beyond v3's retained ablations and JPEG/noise tests.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for the experimental results. The added tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include Seq-DeepFake ACC/F1 of 0.84/0.91, DeepFake localization IoU/F1 of 0.14/0.22, and Tables 8–10's ablation and unseen-generator results. ControlNet and SDXL detection accuracy is 0.99, but ControlNet pixel-level F1 is 0.24 versus HiFi-Net's 0.28. DeepFake dialogue examples gain IoUs and one revised response. Existing benchmark values are largely retained; Table 2's original DFFD entries merely round to two decimals. The learning curve also revises plotted epoch positions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same functional mappings and loss components. Changes clarify prediction versus ground-truth notation, rename the text target, and rearrange equation layout. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's four contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about explainable forgery detection, MMTD-Set, domain-tag guidance, decoupled localization, and broad tampering coverage. New experiments support these existing claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly explains implicit error correction through training on potentially inaccurate detector descriptions and attributes the unsuccessful explicit correction variant to possible interference between text and mask optimization. A.4 interprets the unseen-generator results as generalization evidence. The limitations concerning identity switching and full-face generation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 removes the previously disclosed batch sizes of 24 and 48 while retaining hardware, LoRA settings, learning rates, and epoch counts. New appendix passages document correction supervision, input combinations, and the generators and sample count used for additional testing. The existing repository link moves into the abstract without establishing a change in resource availability.

R1.justification: v4 broadens related-work citations covering copy-move detection, inpainting forensics, and image immunization, and adds references supporting the new baselines and datasets. Section 3.1 cites Huang et al. as methodological inspiration while removing the explicit concurrent-work distinction and old Figure 2 layout acknowledgment. The main novelty positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The revision tightens several methodology and results paragraphs, clarifies notation and captions, and updates affiliations, acknowledgments, and conference headers. Two appendix subsections are inserted and later subsections renumbered. The overall narrative, main section order, and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redesigned to show dataset sources and reference inputs explicitly. v4 adds a main-text dialogue example, extends the localization comparison with a DeepFake column, expands Tables 2, 4, and 6, and adds Tables 8–10. DeepFake dialogue examples gain masks and IoU labels, and the learning curve is redrawn. These materially expand the visual presentation; most remaining appendix figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v4 provides stronger empirical support through additional DeepFake competitors, unseen-generator tests, and targeted architectural ablations, while documenting previously unreported DeepFake localization outcomes. The benefit is limited by sparse descriptions of the new evaluation setups and removal of both batch sizes. Table 10 also qualifies the generalization narrative: FakeShield does not lead ControlNet pixel-level F1. The added evidence yields a useful but limited overall quality improvement.
